clue.text: Snub polar bear

blocks.note: first meaning: a deliberate rebuff or display of coldness towards someone
second meaning, read literally: an Arctic animal's upper foreleg would be chilly

explanation.walkthrough: The second half is whimsical: a polar bear lives on ice, so its shoulder is literally cold.
explanation.definitionFit: Giving someone the cold shoulder is the idiom for ignoring or rebuffing them, which is a snub.

clue.text: Space in plane, male flier on mine

blocks.note: a cock is a male bird
a pit is a coal mine

explanation.surface: A male bird turning up on a mine site, set against the space inside an aircraft.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down clue, 'on' puts the first piece above the second.
explanation.definitionFit: The cockpit is the compartment at the front of an aircraft where the pilot sits.

clue.text: Fruit a disappointment

blocks.note: first meaning: a sour yellow citrus fruit
second meaning: informal for something that turns out to be a dud

explanation.surface: Someone complaining that the fruit they bought was a letdown.
explanation.definitionFit: A dud car or product is colloquially called a lemon, a sense used for any letdown.

clue.text: Story ending in disaster after battle — one should never spill the claret!

definitions.text: one should never spill the claret!

indicators.note: the ending of a word is its final letter, so only that last character of the next word is kept

blocks.note: the Somme was a First World War battle
a lie is a made-up story
the final letter of disaster

explanation.surface: A tale ending badly after a battle, with a bloody aside about not spilling claret, which also means blood.
explanation.walkthrough: 'After battle' puts the battle first. Claret is slang for blood, which suits the battle surface, but here it is the wine.
explanation.definitionFit: A sommelier is a wine waiter, whose professional care is serving wine such as claret without spilling it.

clue.text: Bowling spell finished

blocks.note: first meaning: in cricket, a set of six balls delivered by one bowler
second meaning: ended, done

explanation.surface: A cricket commentator noting that a bowler's spell has ended.
explanation.walkthrough: In cricket an over is a sequence of six deliveries bowled from one end.
explanation.definitionFit: The cricket term names the bowling unit, while the everyday adjective means completed or at an end.

clue.text: Ultimately unusual, parrot able to read and write!

indicators.note: ultimately means at the very end, so just the closing letter of the following word is wanted

blocks.note: the final letter of unusual
to parrot is to repeat, to iterate

explanation.surface: An unusual parrot that can, astonishingly, read and write.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Parrot' looks like the bird but is the verb meaning to repeat.
explanation.definitionFit: Being literate is precisely having the skills of reading and writing.

clue.text: Captured by painter, a topless muse

indicators.note: something captured is held inside, so the letters sit within the following words

blocks.note: the letters run across the end of painter, the word a and the start of topless

explanation.surface: An artist painting a muse who has posed without a top.
explanation.definitionFit: In Greek mythology Erato is one of the nine Muses, presiding over love poetry.

clue.text: This person swallowed by large tiger maybe means to survive

indicators.note: something swallowed ends up inside the swallower, so one piece goes within the other

blocks.note: L is the abbreviation for large
a tiger is an example of a feline; maybe flags the example
the setter referring to themselves

explanation.surface: Someone eaten by a big tiger, morbidly, set beside a way to stay alive.
explanation.walkthrough: 'This person' is the setter, giving I, which goes inside FELINE after its first letter.
explanation.definitionFit: A lifeline is a rope or other resource that offers a way of staying alive or escaping trouble.

clue.text: Wooden pin Margaret left as an example

blocks.note: Peg is a pet name for Margaret
L is the abbreviation for left
e.g. means for example

explanation.surface: Margaret leaving a wooden pin behind to serve as an example.
explanation.definitionFit: Pin is slang for leg, so a wooden pin is an artificial wooden leg.

clue.text: Cheese, part eaten by pet perhaps?

indicators.note: what is eaten ends up inside the eater, so one piece is held within the other

blocks.note: a cat is an example of a pet
a member is a part, such as a limb

explanation.surface: A wedge of cheese partly nibbled by a household pet.
explanation.definitionFit: Camembert is a soft French cheese from Normandy with a white rind.

clue.text: Whispered remark in a camp

blocks.note: taken as written
a camp is a faction or side in a dispute

explanation.surface: A quiet comment murmured within a camp, military or political.
explanation.definitionFit: An aside is a remark made quietly, especially an actor's line meant to be unheard by others on stage.

clue.text: Gambler, one pushing the boat out?

blocks.note: first meaning: a person who places bets
second meaning, read literally: someone propelling a flat boat with a pole

explanation.walkthrough: Pushing the boat out is an idiom for spending lavishly, which fits a gambler; the question mark flags the literal reading of a boatman with a pole.
explanation.definitionFit: A punter is both a bettor and someone who propels a punt, a flat-bottomed river boat, with a pole.

clue.text: Boar surprisingly existing like a bird, for example?

indicators.note: something that happens surprisingly is out of the expected order, so these letters are rearranged

blocks.note: taken as written, to be rearranged
what exists is real

explanation.surface: A wild pig surprisingly living like a bird.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark flags that a bird is only one example of a tree-dwelling creature.
explanation.definitionFit: Arboreal means living in trees, as many birds do.

clue.text: Offence clear, passing backwards in game

indicators.note: going backwards means the letters are read from the end to the start

blocks.note: a sin is an offence
net means clear, as in clear profit

explanation.surface: A sports report of a foul going unpunished in a game.
explanation.walkthrough: To clear a sum is to net it, as in profit after costs.
explanation.definitionFit: Tennis is a racket game played over a net.

clue.text: Bird putting head above opening

blocks.note: nut is slang for head
a hatch is an opening, as in a door or floor

explanation.surface: A bird poking its head out of an opening, like a nest hole.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down clue, 'above' places the first piece on top of the second.
explanation.definitionFit: The nuthatch is a small songbird that climbs tree trunks, often head first.

clue.text: Beautiful but revolting at work?

blocks.note: first meaning: arrestingly attractive
second meaning: workers refusing to work in protest

explanation.walkthrough: 'Revolting' suggests disgusting, the opposite of beautiful; here it means rebelling.
explanation.definitionFit: Striking describes eye-catching good looks, and also workers who are on strike against their employer.

clue.text: Awfully nice, a list difficult to change

indicators.note: something done awfully is done badly and in a mess, so these letters are scrambled

blocks.note: the letters to be rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone praising a list that would be hard to alter.
explanation.definitionFit: Inelastic means rigid and unyielding, as with demand that does not shift with price.

clue.text: Lengthy pain in France?

blocks.note: surface reading: a long-lasting ache suffered while in France
setter's reading: pain is the French word for bread, and this is a long loaf of it

explanation.walkthrough: The English word pain is the French word for bread, so a lengthy French pain is the long thin loaf.
explanation.definitionFit: A long, narrow French bread loaf is exactly what a lengthy piece of French bread describes.

clue.text: Eternal youth in parent brought about by exercise

indicators.note: to bring about is to turn round, so these letters are turned into a different order

blocks.note: PE is physical education
the letters to be rearranged

explanation.surface: A parent kept young by regular exercise.
explanation.walkthrough: 'By' means beside, so the exercise piece sits next to the rearranged parent, here first.
explanation.definitionFit: Peter Pan is J. M. Barrie's boy who never grows up, so his name stands for eternal youth.

clue.text: Work in district, modern style

indicators.note: one thing being in another means it sits inside it

blocks.note: a part is an area or district, as in these parts
op, short for opus, is a work

explanation.surface: A building project in a part of town designed in a contemporary style.
explanation.definitionFit: Pop art is the 1950s and 1960s movement using imagery from popular culture, a modern artistic style.

clue.text: Side with the enemy failing

blocks.note: first meaning: to desert to the opposing side
second meaning: a flaw or shortcoming

explanation.surface: A traitor going over to the enemy and failing in the attempt.
explanation.definitionFit: The verb means to switch allegiance, while the noun means a fault or weakness.

clue.text: Flash starter in tasty seafood

indicators.note: a starter is what comes first, so only the opening letter of the next word is used

blocks.note: the first letter of tasty
a winkle is an edible sea snail

explanation.surface: A quick starter of tasty seafood served up on the menu.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Starter' suggests a first course on a menu, but it means the first letter.
explanation.definitionFit: A twinkle is a brief gleam or flash of light, as in the twinkle of a star.

clue.text: Leader minding language with posh element

indicators.note: minding is looking after, keeping something safely within one's care, so other letters are held inside

blocks.note: the Prime Minister is the national leader
Latin is a language
U means upper-class

explanation.surface: A posh leader watching their language.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Minding' reads as taking care with words, but it means holding inside. U for upper-class or posh is an old British usage.
explanation.definitionFit: Platinum is a precious metallic chemical element, symbol Pt.

clue.text: Contribution made by fashionable set

blocks.note: in means fashionable
to set something down is to put it

explanation.surface: A contribution made by a trendy social set.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Set' looks like a noun for a group of people, but here it is the verb.
explanation.definitionFit: Input is what someone puts in to a discussion or project, so a contribution.

clue.text: Neighbouring characters, one that's a civil rights leader

blocks.note: G and H are neighbouring letters of the alphabet
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: Neighbours being characterised as a civil rights leader.
explanation.walkthrough: The neighbouring characters are written out as words, G AND H.
explanation.definitionFit: Mahatma Gandhi led India's non-violent campaign for independence and civil rights.

clue.text: Play in the morning, a way to get up

indicators.note: in a down entry going up means reading from bottom to top, so the order is turned round

blocks.note: a.m. means in the morning
taken as written
Rd is the abbreviation for road, a way

explanation.surface: Someone playing in the morning as a way to get out of bed.
explanation.definitionFit: A drama is a play for the stage, screen or radio.

clue.text: Post man reported

indicators.note: something reported is spoken of, so the sound of the word counts, not its spelling

blocks.note: a man is a male

explanation.surface: News reported by the postman.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface runs 'Post man' together as postman; the definition is just Post.
explanation.definitionFit: Mail and post are the British and American words for letters and parcels delivered.

clue.text: Summary on top

blocks.note: re means on, concerning
a cap is a top or lid

explanation.surface: A summary placed at the top of a document.
explanation.definitionFit: A recap, short for recapitulation, is a brief summary of what has been said.

clue.text: Item for the breakfast table in oven, hunt sandwiches

indicators.note: a sandwich has its filling between slices, so one piece encloses the other

blocks.note: to track is to hunt down
an oast is a kiln for drying hops

explanation.surface: Sandwiches being made in the oven for a hunt breakfast.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sandwiches' looks like food, fitting the breakfast table, but it is the verb meaning encloses.
explanation.definitionFit: A toast rack is a small stand holding slices of toast upright on the breakfast table.

clue.text: Race arduous, Chelsea given thrashing

indicators.note: a thrashing leaves things beaten about and disordered, so these letters are jumbled

blocks.note: steep means hard going, demanding
the letters to be rearranged

explanation.surface: A football report of Chelsea, the London club, taking a thrashing in a tough contest.
explanation.definitionFit: A steeplechase is a horse or athletics race over fences, ditches and water jumps.
